_comment: ocr LINE-model training profiles. Merge into the rig's training_profiles.json
(/mnt/c/Users/tellt/Projects/orpheus-finetune/training_profiles.json) before a run — that file
is not version controlled, so THIS is the reviewable source of truth. tools/foundry-ocr/train-line.sh
does the merge, and backs the rig's copy up first.
These are NOT tools/foundry-ocr/training-profiles.json. That file holds ocr_v1_4b / ocr_v1_06b,
which train the BLOCK model: input = one OCR block, target = an edit list under the
tools/foundry-ocr/edits.mjs contract. These profiles train the LINE model: input = one band's
Tesseract --psm 7 output, target = the corrected line. Different unit, different corpus
(sft-line/, not sft/), different output contract. Do not cross them.
DERIVED FROM dagger_v1, deliberately, because dagger is the closest cousin that actually
trained and shipped: same base family, same tiny unit of text, same near-verbatim copying,
same chat_jsonl + assistant_only_loss harness. Everything below that differs from dagger_v1
is listed in the description of the profile that changes it, with why.
THREE THINGS ARE NOT NEGOTIABLE:
1. template_kwargs.enable_thinking = false. Qwen3's template with thinking disabled inserts
an empty <think>\n\n</think> block. Train without it and every served prompt is a shape
the model never saw. blocks was bitten by exactly this; dagger_v1 sets it; so do these.
2. load_in_4bit = false. This is character-level copying and quantization costs character
fidelity. A 0.6B in bf16 is ~1.2GB; there is nothing worth saving.
3. JUDGE BY tools/foundry-ocr/eval-line.py, NEVER BY LOSS. Read `degraded` first, every time.
A model that changes nothing and a model that rewrites the author produce the same loss
curve and opposite books.

ocr_line_v1_1_06b.description: ocr v1.1 LINE corrector — ocr_line_v1_06b's recipe EXACTLY, retrained on a re-minted corpus. NOT ONE HYPERPARAMETER DIFFERS from ocr_line_v1_06b: same base, same LoRA, same schedule, same seed 3407, same max_seq_length 512 (re-measured on the new corpus: 47,270 rows give p50 163, p95 181, p99 201, max 246 — identical to v1, zero rows over 512). It exists ONLY so the rebuilt corpus gets its own run id and therefore its own output dir, {run_name}_lora: v1 is being scored and /home/telltale/xtts_ft/ocr_line_v1_06b_lora must survive. WHAT CHANGED IS THE DATA. tools/ocr-lab/align-epub.py commits 9a1666f + 9b417eb re-minted wrap-hyphenated words as a SPLIT: the hyphen line's truth keeps the printed fragment ('ad-') and the continuation line's truth keeps its half ('mit it, ...'). Before 9b417eb the continuation's word-tail was silently DELETED from the truth, so ~17k rows per corpus taught the model to delete a word the scanner had read correctly, and the builder's edge-token rung was papering over it. Measured at the raw mint over the 10 aligned books: the continuation line's truth first word disagreed with the OCR's on 83.5% of hyphen rows before and 7.4% after; the hyphen line's last word, 84.3% before and 6.2% after. In the built corpus the tail-deletion detector falls 126 -> 9 and B-row fragment preservation rises 90.8% -> 94.1%. Downstream in build-dataset.py the hyphen-repair rung is now a no-op on 23,371 of 24,089 rows it fires on (it re-substitutes a fragment the truth already carries), hyphen rows dropped for lack of repair evidence collapse 5,638 -> 932, and whole-edge-word restorations collapse 16,268 -> 3,645 because the aligner no longer produces the artifact they were patching. Corpus: 47,270 train / 21,696 eval / 3,586 eval-german, same holdouts (deathstalker-coda + michelle-remembers), same 50.0% train identity share. The 4 born-digital books aligned by align-pdftext.py (rise-and-fall, gods-people, understanding-jehovahs-witnesses, was-hitler-an-atheist) were deliberately NOT re-minted: that aligner reads truth off PDF text-layer geometry per printed line, so it already emitted hyphens as splits (>99.8%) and re-running align-epub.py on them would swap their truth source, not fix them. STAGE THIS RUN TO ITS OWN REMOTE_DIR (REMOTE_DIR=$HOME/ocr-line-v1_1): the default $HOME/ocr-line holds the corpus v1 was launched against.

ocr_line_v1_1_4b.description: ocr v1.1 LINE corrector at 4B - ocr_line_v1_4b's recipe EXACTLY (Qwen3-4B, batch 2 x accum 8, seed 3407), trained on the re-minted v1.1 corpus (see ocr_line_v1_1_06b for the full corpus story: wrap-hyphens minted as splits, tail-deletions 126 -> 9, hyphen no-evidence drops 5,638 -> 932). Promoted from size control to the v1.1 primary by measurement, Aug 1 2026: scoring ocr_line_v1_06b showed the thin-prior failure this profile's description predicted - unguarded 0.6B is a net NEGATIVE on English headline CER (0.476% vs 0.431% do-nothing), and on the German canary it substitutes rare words with frequent ones at tiny edit distance (Danemark -> Deutschland, Rustung -> Ruckschritt), a CER-invisible factual falsehood that would be narrated. Owner's call: capacity and data over guard machinery. Run id gives its own output dir {run_name}_lora; stage to REMOTE_DIR=$HOME/ocr-line-v1_1 (the default $HOME/ocr-line holds v1's corpus).

ocr_sent_v1_4b.description: ocr SENTENCE corrector v1, Qwen3-4B — the retrain the 2026-08-05 guard measurement asked for. The shipped line model served sentence units repairs LESS and false-edits 12-25% (vs 0.6-7% on lines): a distribution mismatch, and this profile closes it by training on the unit serving actually produces. Corpus: rubric/galley/sft-sent (bookforge 5afef2e) — 31,600 train / 4,979 eval / 770 eval-german sentence units packed from the SAME raw line pairs, holdouts and repair ladder as the line corpus, 50.0% train identity at UNIT level, units p50 331 chars at 4.66 lines each, character-exact eval parity with sft-line asserted by the build. The units were cut by the mirror of foundry src/ocr/sentences.ts (fa4c221: send-more-through boundaries — abbreviation guard incl. German, footnote-reference digits, decimal guard), and serving judges per-run (foundry ab8d303), so training unit == serving unit is a build invariant, not a hope. RECIPE IS ocr_line_v1_1_4b UNCHANGED except max_seq_length 512 -> 768, MEASURED with the real Qwen3 tokenizer, enable_thinking=false: train p50 283 / p90 319 / p99 405 / max 573, eval-german max 579. 23 rows exceed 512 (the tail is German at ~2.2 chars/token — an average-case estimate says 512 holds and is wrong); ZERO exceed 768, and text_sft refuses to truncate, so 512 kills the run partway. STAGE TO REMOTE_DIR=$HOME/ocr-sent-v1. Judge by tools/foundry-ocr/eval-guard.py under per-run against ocr_line_v1_1_4b on the same holdout books, degraded first, do-nothing baseline printed alongside — never by loss. Identity-share sweep variants (0.65/0.8) re-derive from sft-sent/units.jsonl without remining.

ocr_sent_v1_4b_safe.description: FALLBACK for ocr_sent_v1_4b: identical except batch 1 x accum 16, the shape every profile on this box has survived. Same effective batch of 16 so the recipe stays comparable. Exists for the same reason the other _safe profiles do, with the multiplier stated: the OOM ceiling is the lm_head logits tensor (batch x seq x 151936 vocab), and 768 is 1.5x the sequence width the 4B line profile proved at batch 2 — an untested width on a box that measured 11 GB free with a job in it.

ocr_line_v1_06b.description: ocr v1 LINE corrector, Qwen3-0.6B, 16-bit LoRA. Input = one OCR'd line from the band pipeline (render 200dpi -> projection-profile bands -> one tesseract --psm 7 per line); output = the corrected line, or the line unchanged. Sits between recognition and block grouping in docs/OCR_LAB.md's pipeline, which is why the unit is a line and not a block: at this point in the pipeline blocks do not exist yet. Corpus: tools/foundry-ocr/build-dataset.py over <lab>/<book>/scores/epub-align-pairs.json, held out on deathstalker-coda (fiction) + michelle-remembers (nonfiction), train held at 50% identity rows because restraint is the whole game. The holdouts are chosen for what they MEASURE: michelle-remembers is tier-1 publisher truth over a bad IA scan, so its error density is high and informative, and it is the only large book the band pipeline was never tuned against — deathstalker 1 was the calibration book and therefore has to stay in TRAIN, or the score measures the pipeline's own tuning instead of the model. THE MODEL CANNOT SEE THE NEXT LINE, so it is trained to leave a wrap hyphen alone and never to extend the first or last word of a line; the dataset builder enforces both. CHANGED FROM dagger_v1: max_epochs 4 -> 3. dagger took 4 because its corpus was 2,598 rows with one book carrying 98% of the positives; this corpus is ~25k rows across 7+ books, and BLOCKS_TRAINING.md section 5 records that three runs out of three peaked at epoch 1. early_stopping_patience 2 and best-checkpoint selection make 3 a ceiling, not a target. max_seq_length 512 is MEASURED, not assumed: 46,726 train rows through the Qwen3 tokenizer with enable_thinking=false give p50 163, p95 181, p99 201, max 246. Zero rows exceed 512. This matters because text_sft refuses to truncate -- one unmeasured long row kills the run partway through.

ocr_line_v1_06b_safe.description: FALLBACK for ocr_line_v1_06b: identical except batch 1 x accum 16, the shape every profile on this box has survived. Same effective batch of 16 so the recipe stays comparable; step count and wall clock are not. Exists for the same reason dagger_v1_safe does — the OOM ceiling on a small model is the lm_head logits tensor (batch x seq x 151936 vocab), which does not shrink with the model, so an untested batch width is the one thing that can lose a night.

ocr_line_v1_4b.description: SIZE CONTROL for ocr_line_v1_06b, and the owner should expect to need it. Identical corpus and recipe, Qwen3-4B. The block model's profile argues 4B is required because the job is LEXICAL rather than positional, and this corpus makes that concrete: himmler-a-life is now the largest book in TRAIN and its real errors are 'Reichsftihrer' -> 'Reichsfuehrer/Reichsführer', 'Fugoslawien' -> 'Jugoslawien', 'Raterepublik' -> 'Räterepublik' — German proper nouns and umlaut damage, roughly 7,000 edit rows of it. A thin language prior does not merely fail to fix those, it 'corrects' them toward something more English-looking, and the result is narrated. NOTE the holdout change moved the German evidence from eval into train, so the 0.6B's handling of it is no longer measured by the headline: score BOTH sizes and read `degraded` on the German-bearing rows specifically, or the risk goes unobserved. 0.6B is primary only because the pipeline runs this model per LINE, tens of thousands of times per book, where a 4B's inference cost is a real number. batch 2 x accum 8 to match the 4B block profile.
